To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
insulin resistance of large adipocytes is associated with decreased insulin-stimulated GLUT4 translocation and increased intracellular lipid content.

the decreased insulin responsiveness of the large adipocytes of the obese mouse is a consequence of the decreased expression of insulin-responsive glucose transporters and the decreased expression and activity of the glucose transporter translocation machinery, GLUT4.
insulin resistance of large adipocytes is due to a combination of two distinct mechanisms: 1) decreased insulin receptor number, and 2) increased serine phosphorylation of IRS1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of the insulin resistance of large adipocytes in obese animals.
the mechanisms by which large adipocytes become resistant to the action of insulin and how this process is affected by the presence of a high fat diet.
the mechanism(s) by which the insulin responsiveness of the large adipocyte is decreased.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

large adipocytes have decreased insulin responsiveness, which is due to a decrease in the insulin-stimulated glucose transport and a decrease in the glucose oxidation, and that the decreased glucose oxidation is due to a decreased insulin-stimulated GLUT4 translocation.
the insulin resistance of the large adipocytes is caused by an impaired ability of the adipocytes to respond to insulin.
the decreased insulin responsiveness of the large adipocyte is due to a decrease of the number of insulin receptors and to the decreased affinity of the insulin receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
large adipocytes have a decreased insulin responsiveness due to a combination of decreased insulin binding and post-insulin binding events.

large adipocytes have a decreased insulin responsiveness compared to small adipocytes, and that the mechanisms underlying this are related to the decreased insulin sensitivity in the adipocytes, and to the decreased insulin secretion.

insulin resistance of large adipocytes is caused by a combination of decreased insulin receptor number, decreased insulin receptor tyrosine kinase activity, and increased serine phosphorylation of IRS-1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the insulin resistance in large adipocytes is due to the increased levels of intracellular fatty acids.

the large adipocyte population in obese individuals is insulin-resistant and that this insulin resistance is not caused by an inability of the large adipocytes to take up glucose but by the large adipocytes being unable to store glucose as glycogen.
the large adipocytes are more resistant to insulin, and this resistance is mediated by the increased production of reactive oxygen species.
